c1-m1.summary: The user is considering adding an extra room to their house.
c1-m1.source_conv_dialogue:
User: Hi, I'm thinking about my living situation and I was wondering if you could help me explore some ideas.
Assistant: I'd be happy to help. What specifically are you thinking about? Are you looking to move or make some changes to your current setup?
User: Yeah, I'm considering some changes. I've been thinking about what makes a neighborhood or community a good place to live.
Assistant: That's a great question. There are many factors that can contribute to a good living environment. What are some things that are important to you?
User: Well, I think it's nice when families are close together. It can be really convenient and supportive.
Assistant: Having family nearby can be a big plus. It can provide a sense of security and make it easier to get help when you need it.
User: Exactly. And it's not just about the practical benefits. It's also nice to have family members nearby so you can spend time together.
Assistant: Absolutely. Having family close by can be a great way to build relationships and create lasting memories.
User: That's what I'm thinking. But it's not always easy to make it work. Sometimes families have to get creative to find ways to live close together.
Assistant: That's true. Sometimes it requires a bit of thinking outside the box or exploring non-traditional living arrangements.
User: Like, I've seen some families where the grandparents live in a separate house on the same property as their kids and grandkids.
Assistant: That can be a great setup. It allows the grandparents to maintain their independence while still being close to their family.
User: Yeah, I know a family that's actually planning to do something like that. This family can't wait to have their grandparents living next door.
Assistant: That sounds like a wonderful arrangement. I'm sure the grandparents are excited to be so close to their grandkids. How do you think it will work out for them?
User: I think it will be great. The grandparents will be able to help out with childcare and the grandkids will get to spend quality time with them.
Assistant: That's terrific. It's great that they're able to make this arrangement work. Do you think it's something that you would consider for your own family in the future?
User: Yeah, I think it's definitely something I would consider. It's nice to have family close by, and I think it would be really beneficial for everyone involved.
Assistant: Well, it's great that you're thinking ahead and considering what might work best for your family.
User: Hi, I'm looking for some advice on home renovations. I'm planning to make some changes to my house, but I'm not sure where to start.
Assistant: I'd be happy to help! What kind of changes are you thinking of making? Are you looking to add more space, update the interior design, or something else?
User: Actually, I'm thinking of adding an extra room to my house. My in-laws are getting older, and we're considering having them move in with us.
Assistant: That's very thoughtful of you! Adding an in-law suite can be a great way to provide them with a comfortable and private living space. Have you considered the logistics of the addition, such as the cost and the impact on your property value?
User: Yes, we've done some research and spoken to a few contractors. But I'm worried about some potential roadblocks. What are some common issues that people run into when adding an in-law suite?
Assistant: Well, one thing to consider is zoning and local regulations. Some areas have specific rules about adding separate living units to a property. You'll want to make sure you're in compliance with all the relevant laws and regulations.
User: That's a good point. I hadn't thought about that. We do live in a development with a homeowners association (HOA), so I'll need to check with them to see if there are any rules or restrictions.
Assistant: Absolutely! HOAs can have very specific rules about modifications to properties, so it's essential to review your community's bylaws and CC&Rs (Covenants, Conditions & Restrictions) before moving forward.
User: Okay, I'll do that. But what if the HOA has rules against in-law suites? Can they really dictate what I do with my own property?
Assistant: Unfortunately, yes, they can. HOAs have the authority to enforce their rules and regulations, and if you're found to be in non-compliance, you could face fines or other penalties. It's crucial to review your HOA's rules and regulations before starting any project.
User: I see. Well, it turns out that our HOA does have strict rules against in-law suites. I just received a letter from them stating that we're not allowed to add a separate living unit to our property.
Assistant: I'm so sorry to hear that. That must be frustrating for you, especially since you were hoping to provide a comfortable living space for your in-laws. Are you considering appealing the decision or exploring alternative options?
User: Yes, we're not sure what to do next. Do you have any suggestions?
Assistant: Well, you could try appealing the decision to the HOA board, providing them with more information about your plans and how they will benefit the community. Alternatively, you could explore alternative options, such as converting an existing room into a living space for your in-laws or looking into nearby properties that might be more suitable for their needs.
User: Those are some good ideas. Thank you for your advice and guidance. We'll definitely consider our options carefully.
Assistant: You're welcome! I'm glad I could help. Remember to review your HOA's rules and regulations carefully and consider seeking professional advice if you're unsure about any aspect of the process.

User: Hey, I've been thinking about my grandparents a lot lately. What are some ways I can make their lives easier?
Assistant: That's really thoughtful of you! There are many ways to make their lives more comfortable and convenient. Have you considered their current living situation? Are they living with you or in a separate home?
User: They're currently living in a separate home, but it's quite far from us. We have to drive for hours to visit them. I'm worried about their safety and health.
Assistant: I understand your concerns. Having them live far away can be challenging, especially as they age. Have you thought about exploring alternative living arrangements that could bring them closer to you and your family?
User: Actually, yes. We've been discussing that a lot lately. I'm not sure what the best option would be, though. Do you have any suggestions?
Assistant: Well, one possibility could be to consider a multigenerational household, where your grandparents live with or near you and your family. This way, you can keep an eye on them and provide support when needed.
User: That sounds like a great idea. We actually have a big yard with a vacant plot next door. Do you think that could work?
Assistant: Absolutely! Building a separate home or granny flat next door could be an excellent solution. It would allow your grandparents to maintain their independence while still being close to you and your family. What kind of amenities do you think they would need in a new home?
User: Hmm, that's a good question. I think they would need some modifications to make the home senior-friendly, like a walk-in shower and grab bars. And maybe some smart home devices to make things easier for them.
Assistant: Those are all excellent ideas. You may also want to consider factors like natural lighting, wheelchair accessibility, and a simple, intuitive layout to help prevent confusion.
User: Okay, I think we're on the right track. Actually, the family is already preparing a new home for our grandparents next door with all the amenities they need. We're just waiting for the construction to finish.
Assistant: That's fantastic news! It sounds like you and your family are taking proactive steps to create a comfortable and supportive living environment for your grandparents. What are you most looking forward to about having them live next door?
User: I'm excited to spend more quality time with them and make memories. And I know my kids will love having their grandparents nearby. It'll be like having an extended family compound!
Assistant: That sounds wonderful. I'm sure your grandparents will appreciate the love and support, and it'll be a great opportunity for your kids to learn from their wisdom and experiences.
User: Yeah, we're all really excited. But I'm also a bit worried about the transition. Do you have any advice on how to make the move as smooth as possible for them?
Assistant: One thing you might consider is to involve your grandparents in the decision-making process as much as possible, so they feel like they have control over their new environment. You could also try to replicate some of the familiar comforts from their old home in the new one, like favorite furniture or decorations.

Assistant: That's a great question! There are many things that families enjoy doing together, such as going on vacation, playing games, or just having dinner together. Some families also like to share stories and learn about their heritage. What's been on your mind about your family?

Assistant: Absolutely! Learning about their heritage can help kids develop a sense of identity and belonging. It's also a great way to pass down traditions and values from one generation to the next. What kind of things would you like your kids to learn about their heritage?
User: Well, my parents are getting older, and I want to make sure my kids get to spend time with them and hear their stories. But it's hard to find the time with everyone's busy schedules. Do you have any ideas on how to make that work?
Assistant: I totally understand. It can be tough to coordinate everyone's schedules. But having grandparents nearby can make a big difference. Even small moments, like having dinner together or going for a walk, can be really valuable.

Assistant: That sounds like a great plan! Having their grandparents nearby will definitely make it easier for the kids to spend quality time with them. What are you hoping the kids will get out of this experience?
User: Well, like I said, I want them to learn about their heritage and hear stories from my parents. But also, I want them to have a close relationship with their grandparents. I think that's really important for kids.
Assistant: I couldn't agree more. Having a close relationship with grandparents can be incredibly enriching for kids. And it's great that you're thinking about how to make that happen. So, what's the plan for making this move and getting the kids settled in?

Assistant: That sounds amazing! I'm sure it'll be a great experience for everyone involved. And I'm happy to have been a part of your thought process. If you need any more advice or just want to chat, feel free to reach out anytime.

User: The room is about 12 feet by 15 feet. Right now, it's just an empty space with a few boxes and old furniture. We're starting from scratch.
Assistant: With a blank canvas, the possibilities are endless. Let's break down the space into zones. We can have a reading nook, a craft area, and a game table. What do you think about incorporating some storage units to keep the space organized and clutter-free?

c9-m1.summary: The user is a mentor to the assistant.

Assistant: Oh, Mentee. That's very kind of you. Are you sure that you're okay with this?
User: Absolutely. I want you to be happy and healthy, and if that means finding a place of your own, then I'm all for it.
Assistant: Thank you so much, Mentee. You're a true friend.
User: Of course, Mentor. That's what friends are for. Is there anything I can do to help you with the move?
Assistant: Actually, I was hoping you could recommend some neighborhoods or areas to look for apartments.
User: Sure thing. Do you prefer a certain part of town?
Assistant: Well, I love being close to nature, so somewhere with parks or hiking trails nearby would be great.
User: That sounds like my kind of neighborhood too. I'll do some research and send you some recommendations.
Assistant: Thank you, Mentee. You always come through for me.
User: That's what friends are for. Hey, speaking of nature, what ever happened with your family land?
Assistant: Oh, you know, I still have it. It's not worth much, but I love being able to go out there and explore. It's like having my own little slice of paradise.
User: That's really cool, Mentor. Have you discovered anything new out there lately?
Assistant: Actually, I found a hidden stream the other day. It was so peaceful and beautiful. I think I might start going out there more often now.
User: That's awesome. I'm glad you have a place like that to go to and relax. Hey, speaking of discovering new things, have you come up with any new recipes lately?
Assistant: As a matter of fact, I have. I've been experimenting with different herbs and spices, and I think I found the perfect combination for a new pasta dish.
User: Sounds delicious. You'll have to make it for me sometime.
Assistant: I would love to. And thank you again for being such a great friend, Mentee.
User: Anytime, Mentor. That's what friends are for.
User: I don't know what to do. I just received a notice that someone else has claimed the land that has been in my family for generations.
Assistant: That's terrible, I'm so sorry to hear that. What are you going to do?
User: I'm not sure. I mean, it's not worth much, but it's priceless to me. I've always loved exploring the woods and streams on my property.
Assistant: Have you talked to a lawyer about this?
User: Yes, but it's complicated. The person who claimed the land has some sort of legal standing, and it could become a long legal battle.
Assistant: That sounds frustrating. Is there anything I can do to help?
User: Honestly, just having someone to talk to about it helps. It's hard to imagine not having access to that land anymore.
Assistant: I can imagine. It's like losing a part of yourself. But maybe there's some way to reach a compromise or find a solution that works for both parties.

c13-m1.summary: The author had a cordial visit with his estranged grandfather, who he hadn’t seen in twenty years.
c13-m1.source_conv_dialogue:
User: Summarize the story of the author's visit to his estranged grandfather's home and their brief relationship.
Generate according to: I was in my thirties when I visited my grandfather.
It wasn’t the first time I had seen him and wouldn’t be the last, but it had been twenty years since the last time when he came to our home in Jamestown one weekend afternoon after having been to the livestock auction. He introduced himself in an awkward moment.
My mother hadn’t seen her father since she was a teen. He had been around; he just hadn’t been present. The divorce from my grandmother decades earlier had estranged him and poisoned any hope of anything resembling a normal relationship, at least, up to that point.
He went on to remarry and his second wife made sure the loose ends remained untied. His visit to our home was cordial. It was thought of as an invitation to renew a relationship and one, as events later unfolded, was not meant to last nor remain mutually welcomed.
Here I was, however, this time at his home, an old clapboard house on Japa Road with a front porch that spanned the length of the house. A few weathered chairs welcomed guests on occasion. It was a country home, a rural home, a farmer’s home.
He was there along with his wife, my step-grandmother, whom I had never met. She was quiet. She observed with little acknowledgement. That, I learned, was more her way.
“Do you remember me?” I asked stepping on the porch.
He was standing in the open doorway to greet this visitor who stood before him. He didn’t remember me. Of course, I had changed since he had last seen me. I wasn’t the short chubby youth he had met years earlier.
“I am your grandson,” I announced. His eyes grew wide, and he smiled.
I am sure I was the last person he expected to shadow his door. My grandfather and I were more alike than I remembered, more alike than I imagined: short, stocky, thinning hair, and both possibly never strangers to the stinging dullness that life brings.
Perhaps it was the dullness of a long summer’s day that led me to his house, rather than a curiosity about him. Had it been the same that brought him to us those many years ago?
He and I visited. We talked. His wife watched and listened with an apparent indifference. Maybe now would be the time to develop some rapport with him, to obtain some understanding of the man he was as well as the person he wasn’t. No, we wouldn’t go fishing; he wouldn’t take me target shooting or teach me about the plants where the woods meet the clearing’s edge, nor would we relish meals together.
It was just a cordial visit. We talked. It was a visit I still remember with fondness.
When next I saw him, months later, I had changed jobs, and his health had deteriorated.
He had suffered a debilitating stroke and resided in a nursing home where I now worked: a restrictive job surrounded by people I did not know nor care to know, and he possibly the same toward his new surroundings. We were more alike than I imagined.
One day I entered his room, which had been decorated with photos of his children and grandchildren but none of my Mom or of me. I wouldn’t expect there to be photos of us. That old estrangement was still there like a shadow.
I asked him if he remembered me. I looked the same when I had last visited his house. He shook his head. He didn’t remember me.
I found myself feeling indifferent but without judgement toward this man, my mother’s father. Like he once was, now was I – around but not present. There was no need to be present.
He died a few months later. I didn’t go to the service; no notice was published in the local paper. Being alike, I am sure he would not have come to mine either, whether there was an obituary or not.
Perhaps this brief but cordial relationship taught me something about him, more so about the person he wasn’t rather than the man he was. Likewise, it taught me something about the man I was, or perhaps, more importantly, the person I wasn’t.
Darrell Gooding was born in Fentress County, Tennessee, on the Cumberland Plateau where his family has resided for several generations. Gooding graduated from Tennessee Technological University with a master’s degree in Educational Psychology. His work in the social service field eventually brought him to East Tennessee where he has resided for the past ten years.

The grandfather passed away a few months later, and the author did not attend the service. The brief relationship taught the author something about both his grandfather and himself.

c15-m1.summary: Fact 1: Leaders in government should prioritize policies that address underlying needs and honor service members and their families.

User: Read the passage below and answer the question or follow the instruction: What actions do you believe leaders in government should take to better serve and honor our veterans and their families? Passage: More than 25 years ago, my Great Uncle, Zachary Fisher and his wife, Elizabeth, opened the first Fisher House to provide ‘a home away from home’ for families of wounded, injured or ill service members traveling far from home for medical treatment. They did it not just because they saw a great need, but because they knew that when it comes to our veterans, saying “thank you for your service” just isn’t enough. Every time I turn on my television, I’m reminded that we live in an uncertain time. As a native New Yorker, I’m saddened and devastated by the senseless act of terror that occurred in my city recently. As an American, I’m frustrated by the dialogue surrounding our service members and veterans in the media and on the national stage. Most importantly, I’m driven by the conviction that we owe a tremendous debt to those who have answered the call to put themselves in harm’s way to keep us safe. With Veterans Day on the horizon, I think about the hundreds of thousands of families who have stayed in Fisher Houses over the last two and half decades. If they were still here today, Zach and Elizabeth would be so proud to see 72 homes across the country, but they would be amazed by the resilience, pride and strength of the heroes and families who have benefitted from them. Heroes like Will Reynolds, who was injured when an IED exploded and ultimately took his left leg above the knee. We were there for him and his family during months of surgeries and rehabilitation, and we were also there to celebrate his triumphs as he persevered through his injuries to participate in the Warrior Games and the Invictus Games as team captain. I also think about the unsung heroes. The families — moms, dads, spouses, children — who made sacrifices during deployment and continue to give their all through recovery. Women like Minie Curry, whose husband Anson suffered traumatic and permanent brain injury in Afghanistan from a grenade explosion. Minie stayed with us in Palo Alto for nine months during Anson’s recovery and is the true embodiment of the vow ‘in sickness and in health’. We were there with Minie and Anson during the difficulties of treatment, but also during the joy when they renewed their wedding vows. For all of the Wills and Minies in our country, “thank you for your service” isn’t enough. One day of celebration isn’t enough. We owe everything to these brave men and women, and for my part, I’m going to continue building on my aunt and uncle’s legacy through continuing to make Fisher House a beacon and safe haven for our veterans, service members and their families. We all have a role to play when it comes to serving those who have served us. Leaders in government on both sides of the aisle need to set an example for how to honor and respect the brave men and women fighting for their freedoms. They must stop using veterans and their families as political footballs and instead channel their energies into creating policies that address underlying needs and both protect and honor service members and their families. The time for talk and empty promises must end. We must keep veteran’s issues in the forefront so that every day is Veterans Day, not just Nov. 11. We have our own call of duty to ensure that our veterans receive that which they have earned — a system that cares for them and a nation that truly honors service and sacrifice, because “thank you for your service” is not enough.

2. Education and Job Training: Leaders in government can promote and create opportunities for veterans to get higher education or job training, which will help them obtain well-paying jobs and re-integrate themselves into society.

3. Healthcare Services: Healthcare services for veterans can provide top-notch care for the men and women who have served to protect the country. The government should provide adequate funding to ensure that veterans have access to proper medical care.

4. Affordable Housing: The government can implement more affordable housing options so that veterans and their families have a stable and affordable place to live.

5. Increase Disability Compensation: Government can increase funding for disability compensation, which is provided to veterans who suffer from disability or injuries sustained while in active-duty service. This will help them to cope and have a better quality of life. 

These are just some examples of how government leaders can take action and implement policies and programs to better serve and honor our veterans and their families.

The organization aims to provide a sense of warmth and comfort to the families during often-difficult situations. It is open to all branches of the military.

The organization is focused primarily on helping veterans and their families with critical medical needs. Fisher House provides a safe, convenient, and comfortable place for these families to stay while their loved ones are receiving medical treatment. This relieves the financial and emotional burden on family members who would otherwise need to arrange and pay for lodging, food, and travel to be near their loved ones.

We will be there until after the New Year to visit with family and friends but it won't be that same. This is something I knew I would have to face at some point but it's still hard. I have been busy thinking up new family traditions to pass along to our kids and hopefully someday we will be back home with our family. Dreams to come true, we just have to believe it will happen. Merry Christmas everyone!

c57-m1.source_conv_dialogue:
User: What a strange and wonderful journey we've been on in 2013…. Oh, wait, what's that? We're not at Nov. 31st already? Oh ya, that's right we're just giving you a look from the beginning of the calendar year as to what each of Wisconsin's opponents could present as challenges or lack thereof.
With that, let's get right into our friends from Happy Valley, shall we?
Crazy 2012 Stat: 13 - That's the total number of interceptions and lost fumbles by the Nittany Lions in 2012. For a team that had so many issues with turnovers in 2011 with virtually the same cast of characters in games in 2012 that turnaround, especially from Matt McGloin was unreal.
What 2012 Tells Us About Penn State: If 2012 proved anything, it's that Penn State - the football team - won't roll over and play dead just because they are hamstrung with sanctions and a lack of postseason play. In fact they're likely to do the opposite. But, that was 2012 and a group of players and leaders that were rather special. Can they repeat those leadership qualities with the likes of Michael Mauti gone?
What about their head coach? Is Bill O'Brien actually committed to this university or is it all about jumping to the NFL as quickly as possible? Those are big time questions as we head into 2013 and this season could go a long way to showing us the true motives and intentions of the coach.
However, what 2012 told us about the team on the field is that this isn't JoePa's team anymore. They're going to be a much more aggressive offense and a much more pass happy offense as well. On defense they're just going to build off of what's worked so well for them in the past 40 years and not much changed in year one of the BO'B era because of that.
One thing is for sure, we'll know exactly what we're in for - either a challenge or a team not looking forward to playing - because it's the season ending game between the Badgers and Nittany Lions.
WAY Too Early Prediction: Wisconsin 27, Penn State 17 - This is a tough, TOUGH football game to predict. There are a lot of really talented players returning for the Nittany Lions and this series has been hard to predict because blowouts and upsets have been common and not seen coming either. However, looking at this game in January there is one big time hole in the PSU program that needs to be filled and that's at quarterback. Yes, PSU has a big time recruit in Christian Hackenberg, but there's a big time jump from high school to the top levels of college football. Either way they'll be looking at starting a completely unproven guy at quarterback - a position that is vitally important to the success of Bill O'Brien's system. Call me crazy but the Badgers defense should be good enough to deal with a team that didn't run the ball well last season & has lost all of it's best talent from a season ago on the defensive side of the ball. It will be close though.
SEASON THOUGHTS: So, that means we're seeing a Badgers team that will be 11-1 to end the regular season - does that mean another trip to Indianapolis for Wisconsin? It could depending on what the Buckeyes do. What's the worst case scenario we see happening for this team? Losses to ASU and Northwestern are certainly possible so at a worst case scenario we see the Badgers as a 9-3 team with a ceiling of 11-1 in Gary Andersen's 1st year at the helm.
What are the best and worst case scenarios for the Badgers in the 2013 season and what factors contribute to those outcomes?
Assistant: Best case scenario for the Badgers would be to finish the season with a perfect 12-0 record, win the Big Ten Championship game and earn a spot in the College Football Playoff. To achieve this, the team would need consistent play from their quarterback, a dominant running game, and a strong defense. They can also benefit from favorable scheduling, with Ohio State being a home game and Michigan State having to replace key players on offense.

On the other hand, the worst case scenario for Wisconsin would be a 6-6 record and no bowl game. This would likely come from inconsistent quarterback play, a lack of depth at certain positions, and tough losses on the road against teams like Nebraska and Minnesota.

Factors that could contribute to these outcomes include the development of the new quarterback, the ability of the defense to replace key players, injuries, and overall team chemistry. Coaching decisions and game preparation could also play a role in the success or failure of the season.

A loyalist to Chun Li, Mov was a 3rd Strike Legend. Honing his skills, his Chun Li is intensely scary and his knowledge of every matchup is unparalleled. He’s in Top 8 at almost any tournament you’ll see him in, and he is extremely expressive. MOV is fun to watch.
Filipino Champ is another of the United States' best. Arguably the best Dhalsim player in the world, and one of the best overall fighting game players in the world. Watching fChamp is watching somebody get taken down through a war of attrition. His knowledge of when to go in vs when to stay back is unrivaled, and, he has some pretty fun pop offs as well.
Hailing from Korea, the fact that Infiltration isn’t qualified is actually pretty shocking. He started Street Fighter V Season 1 in a dominating fashion, but being considered almost unbeatable. Through a few balance patches, he’s had to find his way back, but based on what he showed at some local tournaments in Anaheim he’s ready to turn some heads. In my mind, he’s one of the top choices to win this last chance qualifier, and if he does, it could cause a lot of upsets at the finals this weekend.

OK, once the last chance qualifiers are over on Friday, everyone can start preparing for the big show tomorrow. Literally, every player in this tournament is a killer, so instead of giving you notable names to follow, instead, I’ll give you some formatting rules and basic terms to get you up to speed.
This is a double elimination tournament. If you’re not familiar with that format, losing when in the “winners bracket” sends you to losers, where another loss eliminates you. It is possible to lose both matches pretty quick, and that happens to 50% of the players entering.
Matches are 2/3 until Top 8. This means each set is 2/3 to win a match, and each match is 2/3.
Punish: In fighting games, there are moves that leave you at a disadvantage or “negative” what this means is that you have done something that leaves you exposed and your opponent has a move that is fast enough that it is a guaranteed to hit. If you leave yourself exposed and they hit you for the free damage that’s a punish.
Whiff punish: This type of punish is more technical. Essentially, if you push a button (punch/kick) referred to as a normal, and your opponent positions themselves correctly, they can push a button that will hit yours during recovery (the time it takes for the animation to finish out). This is called whiff punishing.
Combo: a series of moves linked together for more damage.
Damage scaling: In Street Fighter, combos lead to scaling. What this means is that the damage of a move is reduced with each hit in a combination. This helps reduce the chance of one combo kills and the like.
Reset: This is something that happens when a combo can be dropped in a precarious position for your opponent. Maybe its something that forces a side switch and they have to guess which side you are going to land on, maybe they are mashing out a special move during your combo and you drop and block to get a new punish. Whatever it is, a reset is essentially dropping a combo and resetting the scaling to get more damage.
Mashing: This is exactly what it sounds like, your opponent was hitting something either during a block string, or on wakeup, they are “mashing” the buttons to make something happen.
I hope you find this beginners guide mildly helpful. There are a ton of resources you can check out to find more information. And, if you’re a stat junkie like myself you can follow along at Smash.gg to see who’s winning where. They also have a really fun contest going, where you are given a budget and can pick 8 “fantasy players” depending on how far those players make it in the tournament you will get points and the winner gets some swag.
If you’re in Anaheim and have some free time today, I highly recommend getting to the venue and watching the action live.

User: How can budgeting on a weekly and annual basis help save money? Answer according to: Do you know how much you can afford to spend each month? Or do you lie awake at night worrying how you’ll pay for everything? Read four tips to help you you keep on top of household bills.
Even though our household bills are apparently rising more slowly than the rate of inflation, it can be tough keeping on top of them. And often it’s not the large outgoings like mortgage or rent that catch us out, but the many smaller bills that can easily add up each month if we don’t keep an eye on them.
So if you’re sick of running out of money each month, or dread checking your online statement, what can you do?
The best way to prevent any problems when it comes to household bills is to get ahead of them. Here are four tips to help you keep on top of your finances, and end your monthly money worries.
The first step is to understand just how much money you have to work with, and what expenses you can (and need to) reliably plan for. Make a list of all your incomings, and another of your essential, fixed cost regular outgoings, like mortgage, utility bills, car payments etc. From this, work out how much money you will always have left over each month.
Now check these costs work with the amount of money you actually have to spend. If not, adjust them. Don’t forget to leave a buffer each month for unexpected expenses.
By getting into the habit of budgeting you can see where you can afford to spend more, and where you need to cut back. You’ll also be ahead of any unpleasant financial surprises!
Don’t wait for sudden expenses to hit. When you’re creating your budget, think of the year ahead. Are there times you’ll need more money? Christmas, birthdays and holidays, for example? Or when your car insurance renewal comes around (if you pay annually)?
And what about school? Are any big trips coming up? Don’t forget buying uniform for a new school year, too. Try to include any annual expenses you think may come up.
You can also plan ahead on a weekly basis to save money – for example by meal planning. We’re wasting more money than ever by throwing unused food away. So a quick and easy way to add money back into your monthly budget is to plan ahead for your meals each week. This way you’ll only shop for ingredients you’ll definitely use.
This also gives you another saving – time! Instead of wasting time every evening staring into a fridge and wondering what you can pull together into a meal, you’ll know exactly what to do. If you really want to get one step ahead, you’ll plan some meals you can pre-prepare on a Sunday and freeze, ready to pull out the day you need them.
There are many different ways you can cut down on your weekly and monthly costs. For example, if you drive to work can you car share with a colleague? Or even walk or cycle?
And what about your bills? Are you really getting the best deals? It’s worth shopping around using online calculators to find out. Sometimes even just calling a provider and asking if you’re on the best deal is worth doing. It may be they’ve added a new, better value deal, or you’re not using everything you’re currently paying for.
And what about food and toiletries? Are you shopping smartly? Could you get the same or similar products from another shop, or online? Are you buying things you don’t need or throw away? Even just small savings here and there can add up to a significant sum over time.
And finally, don’t let taking control of your bills be a one-off exercise. By using an ongoing spreadsheet (or an online financial tool) to keep track of what you’re spending each week, you’ll always be on top of what’s coming in and going out. You’ll know when you need to cut back, and when you can afford to splash out without guilt.
And you can make sure you have enough put by for any sudden expenses (like moving home or a big car repair), so you don’t need to lie awake at night worrying where you’re going to find the money.

User: The Columbia Gorge is one of the most beautiful places to go for a hike. Take your backpack, some snacks, and bring the family for a day adventure. Multnomah Falls not only is the tallest falls in Oregon, but there are several fun hikes around the area, like Wahkeena Loop Hike.
Portland Farmers Market at Portland State University’s campus is known as one of the best Market’s in the Pacific Northwest. There are over 200 vendors selling everything from flowers, meats, cheeses, baked goods, fruits, vegetables and some of Portland’s best food carts. Stop by the market on Saturday before breakfast to beat the crowd, or coming later in the day to shop and eat. Portland Farmers Market PSU runs through December.
Take a drive up to Mount Hood and check out the historic Timberline Lodge. This National Historic Landmark sits at an elevation of 5960 feet in the beautiful Mount Hood National Forest. Go for a day hike around Mount Hood and come back to Timberline for a fun dining experience.
Put on your pajamas, grab the kids, and head to Hood River for the Polar Express Train. Drink hot cocoa, eat some cookies all while listening to the Polar Express story. The train takes you through the beautiful Hood River Valley, with a quick stop at The North Pole. Before the trip ends, there is a very special guest that hops on the train giving every child a unique Christmas gift.
The Japanese Garden located in Portland, Oregon is one of the most unique and beautiful destinations in Portland. This garden sits on more than 5.5 acres. This is a great activity for the whole family that even the kids will enjoy.
Attend the 40th Northwest Filmmakers Festival now through November 16th in Portland. Join in this celebration and support our regional filmmakers and artists. To attend one of the special screenings, check out the NW Film Center Center schedule. User: Hey, B! I just finished reading your book, "The Life of an Inspiring Woman." It was amazing and truly inspiring.
Assistant: Thank you so much, A! I'm glad you enjoyed it.
User: Your story has motivated me to become an inspiring woman myself. I want to make a difference in people's lives, just like you did.
Assistant: That's so wonderful, A! I'm sure you'll be able to inspire many people in your own unique way.
User: I wanted to ask, how did you stay motivated when faced with challenges and obstacles in your life?
Assistant: It was difficult at times, but I always remembered my purpose and why I was doing what I was doing. Having a strong support system also helped me stay motivated.
User: That makes a lot of sense. I definitely think having a support system is important. Thank you for sharing that with me.
Assistant: Of course, A. Do you have any plans on how you want to become an inspiring woman?
User: I'm not sure yet, but I'm thinking of starting by volunteering in my community and helping out where I can. I also want to work on improving myself and my own skills, so I can be of more help to others.
Assistant: Those are great ideas, A. Starting small is a great way to build up to bigger goals.
User: Yes, I agree. I'm excited to see where this journey takes me. And thanks again for inspiring me with your book.
Assistant: You're welcome, A. I'm excited to see where your journey takes you as well.
User: , have you been keeping up with the news lately?
Assistant: Not really, to be honest. I've been so focused on my studies that I haven't had much time to read the news.
User: I understand, but I think it's important to stay informed about what's going on in the world. I read The New York Times every morning to stay up to date.
Assistant: That's a good idea. I should start doing that too. What kind of articles do you like to read?
User: I enjoy reading the opinion section to learn about different points of view. It helps me to broaden my perspective and think critically about important issues.
Assistant: That's interesting. Speaking of broadening perspectives, remember when you wanted to be as smart as me in class?
User: Yes, I do remember. I admired your intelligence and wanted to learn from you. That's why I started paying more attention in class and studying harder outside of school.
Assistant: Well, it looks like your hard work paid off. You're now the head of the committee and making positive changes.
User: Thank you for saying that. I'm passionate about making a difference and it's great to be able to do it as the head of the committee.
Assistant: It's inspiring to see you strive for excellence and make a difference. Speaking of making a difference, have you learned anything new about the environment lately?
User: Yes, actually. I've been reading a lot of books and watching documentaries to learn more about how the environment affects animals and plants. It's fascinating how everything is interconnected.
Assistant: That's really cool. It's important to learn more about the environment so we can take care of it and preserve it for future generations.
User: Absolutely. I think it's important that we all do our part in taking care of our planet.

User: Analyze the similarities and differences between the adaptations of books, comics, and graphic novels into movies. Explore how the change in medium affects the story, characterization, and themes. Discuss which adaptations stayed faithful to the source material and which ones took creative liberties. Evaluate how successful these adaptations are in appealing to both fans of the original material and a wider audience.
Assistant: When it comes to adapting books, comics, and graphic novels into movies, there are both similarities and differences. One similarity is that these adaptations often involve condensing the source material into a shorter format in order to fit into a typical 2-hour movie runtime. However, the way that this is done can vary significantly based on the medium being adapted.

In the case of books, the biggest challenge is often condensing a sprawling narrative with numerous characters and subplots into a linear storyline that can fit into a movie. This often means that characters and events may be cut, combined, or simplified in order to streamline the narrative. The themes and messages of the book may also be shifted in order to make the story more cinematic or to appeal to a wider audience.

With comics and graphic novels, the adaptation process can be a bit different, as these media often involve visual storytelling that is closer to the language of film. However, translating the style and tone of the original work into a movie can still be a challenge, particularly if the source material has a distinct visual style or structure that is difficult to replicate on screen. Many comic book adaptations have also struggled with how to balance the more fantastical elements of the source material with a more grounded, realistic approach that can appeal to a wider audience.

One of the key differences between these mediums is the level of detail that can be conveyed. Books allow for a significant amount of internal monologue and introspection, while comics and graphic novels can convey a great deal of information through visual cues and panel layout. Movies, on the other hand, are inherently more limited in the amount of detail they can convey, particularly when it comes to characters' thoughts and emotions. This can lead to adaptations that feel more action-focused and less character-driven than the source material.

In terms of faithfulness to the source material, there are examples of both faithful adaptations and those that take creative liberties. Some adaptations, such as the Harry Potter series or the recent Netflix adaptation of The Queen's Gambit, hew closely to the books they are based on, reproducing key scenes and dialogue in almost exact detail. Other adaptations, such as Zack Snyder's Watchmen or the recent Joker movie, take significant liberties with the source material in order to tell a different kind of story or to update the themes for a modern audience.

Ultimately, the success of an adaptation is often measured by how well it appeals to both fans of the original material and a wider audience. Some adaptations, such as The Lord of the Rings trilogy or the Marvel Cinematic Universe, have managed to become cultural touchstones that appeal to both fans of the source material and those who have never read the books or comics they are based on. Others, such as the recent Dark Tower movie, have struggled to please either fans or newcomers, leading to disappointment for both groups.

In conclusion, the process of adapting books, comics, and graphic novels into movies requires balancing the strengths and limitations of each medium, condensing and reworking the source material to fit into a more limited format, and often making creative choices that can either enhance or detract from the original work. The most successful adaptations are those that balance faithfulness to the source material with a strong sense of cinematic storytelling, appealing to both fans of the original material and a wider audience.

The view of the old growth forest from the ship.
Caves formed by wave erosion.
And you will find various cliffs in strange shapes.
Shiretoko enjoys its abundant water resources, and you can see the sceneries with waterfalls formed by the water on the cliffs flowing out of sources including Shiretoko Goko lakes here and there.
You can observe a wide variety of birds including the white-tailed eagles, the Steller’s sea eagles, and the Japanese cormorants.

Kayaking tour offers you better experience of the nature offered by Shiretoko than that from the ship.

Generate according to: Shiretoko Peninsula which is situated on the eastern part of Hokkaido is a tourist destination blessed with abundant nature, where it was registered as another World’s natural heritage site in 2005.Sightseeing of the old growth forest in Shiretoko Peninsula, and the vastly extensive coastline facing the steep cliffs are popular tourist attractions. The roundtrip cruise lasts for three hours from the loading dock to Cape Shiretoko.
The view of the old growth forest from the ship.
Caves formed by wave erosion.
And you will find various cliffs in strange shapes.
Shiretoko enjoys its abundant water resources, and you can see the sceneries with waterfalls formed by the water on the cliffs flowing out of sources including Shiretoko Goko lakes here and there.
You can observe a wide variety of birds including the white-tailed eagles, the Steller’s sea eagles, and the Japanese cormorants.
And… the brown bears make frequent appearances!
And, let’s not to forget about Cape Shiretoko, the tip of the Shiretoko Peninsula. Although there is a lighthouse at the cape, you can only see it from the sea as there is no land access.
If you are lucky, you can see dolphins and whales while you are on this cruisetour. In addition, there are tours that let you play on the drift ice during the winter time!
There are also tours that let you experience the up-close view of cliffs by kayaking right along the coastline.
Kayaking tour offers you better experience of the nature offered by Shiretoko than that from the ship.
Fukiage onsen makes the best soak for free!
Assistant: Yes, there are alternative tours available to experience the nature of Shiretoko Peninsula besides the roundtrip cruise. Some of these tours include kayaking along the coastline to get an up-close view of the cliffs, playing on drift ice during winter, and sightseeing of the old growth forest and extensive coastline. You can also observe various birds including the white-tailed eagles, Steller’s sea eagles, and Japanese cormorants. Furthermore, there are hot springs like Fukiage onsen that allow visitors to soak and relax for free.
User: Can you provide more information on the kayaking tour along the coastline of Shiretoko Peninsula? Where can I book this tour?
Assistant: Sure! The kayaking tour along the coastline of Shiretoko Peninsula is a popular way to experience the nature here up-close. You will be able to witness the unique and breathtaking rock formations, waterfalls, and other sights on this tour. The kayaking tour is usually led by an experienced guide who will ensure your safety and teach you some basic kayaking techniques if needed.

There are several tour operators who offer kayaking tours in Shiretoko Peninsula. Some of the popular ones include Shiretoko Adventure World, Shiretoko Nature Cruise, and Shiretoko Goko Nature Center. You can book these tours online through their websites or by contacting them directly.

The kayaking tour usually lasts for around 2 to 3 hours and costs around 5,000 to 8,000 JPY per person. It is recommended to book in advance as these tours can fill up quickly during peak tourist season. Also, make sure to dress appropriately for kayaking and follow the safety guidelines provided by your tour operator.
